child_briefs.title: Enforcement integration: mode-switch lock, action sequence-lock, phase guidance
child_briefs.scope: Additively edit three EXISTING overseer symbols (one file per leaf) so the substrate's procedure machine WITHHOLDS out-of-order actions and mode switches rather than discouraging them, preserving every current behaviour and passing test. (1) EDIT overseer/mode_gate.py::can_switch — while the conversation's active procedure phase is not the terminal COMPLETE, return False for EVERY target except observe (the always-available abort that abandons the procedure) and current (no-op); once the phase reaches COMPLETE the existing lattice rules resume unchanged. (2) EDIT overseer/actions.py::dispatch_action — add a fail-closed (phase, command) check BESIDE the existing (mode, command) check: a command not permitted by the CURRENT phase is REFUSED with a ModeViolation BEFORE any seam fires, and the current phase's gate must PASS before the phase advances. (3) EDIT overseer/mode_prompts.py::render_mode_context — render the state-derived CURRENT phase, the last gate's pass/fail plus its fix_hint, and the SINGLE next action, all read from durable procedure state and never inferred. Extend the existing oracles tests/overseer/test_mode_gate_sequence.py (new), test_actions.py, and test_mode_prompts.py as the per-leaf verification_command targets.
child_briefs.non_goals: Do NOT author the substrate (gates.py, procedure.py, procedure_state.py) — consume it. Do NOT touch run_chat_turn or the PreToolUse hook (the runtime_wiring child owns those). No new agent spawns, model/API/network/SSE calls, or un-injected subprocesses. No changes to harness/** or the autowork daemon. No procedures or registry entries for the out-of-scope modes. The word 'integration' is load-bearing here: these are EXISTING-symbol additive edits that must preserve all current behaviour and tests, each leaf editing exactly ONE file (no multi-file emission). This child does not dispatch a build or author the production oracles.
child_briefs.inputs: From procedure_substrate: PROCEDURE_REGISTRY (mode name -> ordered phases, each phase binds a gate name + next-action string); advance(procedure, phase, gate_result) -> Decision (next phase | Blocked(reason, fix_hint) | Complete); GateResult(ok: bool, reason: str, fix_hint: str); ProcedureState(phase: str, last_gate: GateResult | None) with load_state(conversation_id, *, state_dir) -> ProcedureState and save_state(conversation_id, state, *, state_dir) -> None. The ALREADY-BUILT seams being edited: overseer/mode_gate.py::can_switch(current, target, unlocked), overseer/actions.py::dispatch_action(mode, command, args, *, seams), overseer/mode_prompts.py::render_mode_context(mode, state), and the ModeViolation exception type already raised by dispatch_action.
child_briefs.deliverables: Edited overseer/mode_gate.py whose can_switch consults the active procedure phase and returns False for all targets except observe/current while phase != COMPLETE, resuming the existing lattice once phase == COMPLETE. Edited overseer/actions.py whose dispatch_action raises ModeViolation on a (phase, command) pair not permitted by the current phase, before any seam fires, beside the existing (mode, command) fail-closed check. Edited overseer/mode_prompts.py whose render_mode_context emits the current phase, last GateResult pass/fail + fix_hint, and the single next-action string from durable procedure state. Oracles tests/overseer/test_mode_gate_sequence.py (new), test_actions.py (extended), and test_mode_prompts.py (extended), each named as a leaf verification_command python -m pytest tests/overseer/<oracle>.py -q.
child_briefs.interfaces: Consumes PROCEDURE_REGISTRY; advance(procedure, phase, gate_result) -> Decision; GateResult(ok: bool, reason: str, fix_hint: str); ProcedureState(phase: str, last_gate: GateResult | None); load_state(conversation_id, *, state_dir) -> ProcedureState. Edits can_switch(current, target, unlocked), dispatch_action(mode, command, args, *, seams), render_mode_context(mode, state) additively, preserving their existing signatures and behaviour.

child_briefs.title: Deterministic procedure substrate: gates, phase reducer, durable state
child_briefs.scope: Build the three NEW, pure/stdlib-only, single-file whole-file modules that encode the operator recipe as checked machinery, each over INJECTED seams and never spawning a process or making a model/API/network/SSE/un-injected subprocess call. (1) overseer/gates.py — one pure gate-check function per lesson, each returning a typed GateResult(ok, reason, fix_hint): oracle_is_red(test_path, *, run_seam) asserting the named test FAILS; oracles_committed_at_head(paths, *, git_seam) asserting each oracle path is committed at HEAD not merely on disk; brief_lint(brief_text) checking the brief contains '# Required plan shape', names exactly one target file, has no naked source line-number citations, and is single-file scope; plan_preflight(plan, *, state_dir) WRAPPING (not reimplementing) harness.planner.plan_validator and additionally checking a unique non-'T1' task_id with no state/tasks/processed/<id>.json collision, >=2 edge_cases reflected in regression/property tests, and the literal word 'integration' in non_goals; suite_green_zero_reg(report) asserting the named oracle is GREEN and the full suite shows 0 new regressions vs baseline; posture_locked(*, state_dir) asserting state/control/autowork/full_stop present, state/control/orchestrator.flag==pause, and state/control/autowork/auto_promote.allowlist deny-all. (2) overseer/procedure.py — Phase/Procedure dataclasses, the PROCEDURE_REGISTRY holding the four mode->ordered-phase definitions (brief-author: SCOPE->ORACLE->COMMIT->BRIEF->PLAN->COMPLETE; oracle-author: SCOPE->DRAFT->RED->COMMIT->COMPLETE; dispatch: PREFLIGHT->STAGE->BUILD->VERIFY->RESTORE->COMPLETE; push: SWEEP->ZERO_REG->POSTURE->PUSH->COMPLETE), each phase binding a gate by name plus a single next-action string, and the pure reducer advance(procedure, phase, gate_result) -> Decision returning the next phase, a Blocked(reason, fix_hint), or Complete. (3) overseer/procedure_state.py — durable per-conversation phase pointer plus recorded gate results, read not reconstructed and surviving --resume/restart. Author each module's hand-written RED oracle expectations under tests/overseer/ (test_gates.py, test_procedure.py, test_procedure_state.py) as the per-leaf verification_command targets.
child_briefs.non_goals: No edits to existing overseer symbols (can_switch, dispatch_action, render_mode_context, run_chat_turn) — those belong to the enforcement and runtime children. No new agent spawns, model/API/network/SSE calls, or un-injected subprocesses: all test execution, HEAD membership, and filesystem I/O flow through injected seams (run_seam, git_seam, plain fs reads / state_dir). Do NOT reimplement harness.planner.plan_validator — wrap it. No changes to harness/** or the autowork daemon. No registry entries or procedures for the out-of-scope modes (triage/daemon-supervisor/ui-tester/flag-steward/harness-self-fix/security-review/rebuild-factory) — substrate stays generic so they can adopt a procedure later by adding a registry entry only. This child authors the decomposition's substrate leaves only; it does not dispatch a build or author the production oracles (those are hand-authored and committed before any leaf is dispatched).
child_briefs.inputs: The seven operator lessons in the epic Scope (one lesson per gate). The committed ALREADY-BUILT overseer foundation as fixed read-only seams: overseer/modes.py (ModeSpec, MODE_REGISTRY, get_mode, list_available_modes), overseer/mode_gate.py, overseer/mode_prompts.py, overseer/actions.py, overseer/driver.py, overseer/turn_runner.py, overseer/session_store.py, overseer/transcript.py. The existing harness.planner.plan_validator (wrapped by plan_preflight). The posture flags under state/control/: state/control/autowork/full_stop, state/control/orchestrator.flag, state/control/autowork/auto_promote.allowlist (read by posture_locked).
child_briefs.deliverables: overseer/gates.py exposing the dataclass GateResult(ok: bool, reason: str, fix_hint: str) and the gate functions oracle_is_red(test_path, *, run_seam) -> GateResult, oracles_committed_at_head(paths, *, git_seam) -> GateResult, brief_lint(brief_text) -> GateResult, plan_preflight(plan, *, state_dir) -> GateResult, suite_green_zero_reg(report) -> GateResult, posture_locked(*, state_dir) -> GateResult. overseer/procedure.py exposing the Phase and Procedure dataclasses, the PROCEDURE_REGISTRY mapping the four mode names (brief-author, oracle-author, dispatch, push) to ordered phase lists where each phase binds a gate name and a next-action string, and the pure reducer advance(procedure, phase, gate_result) -> Decision where Decision is the next phase string, a Blocked(reason, fix_hint), or Complete. overseer/procedure_state.py exposing a ProcedureState carrying phase: str and last_gate: GateResult | None, plus load_state(conversation_id, *, state_dir) -> ProcedureState and save_state(conversation_id, state, *, state_dir) -> None. Each module's RED oracle under tests/overseer/ (test_gates.py, test_procedure.py, test_procedure_state.py) named as the leaf verification_command python -m pytest tests/overseer/<oracle>.py -q.
child_briefs.interfaces: GateResult(ok: bool, reason: str, fix_hint: str); oracle_is_red(test_path, *, run_seam) -> GateResult; oracles_committed_at_head(paths, *, git_seam) -> GateResult; brief_lint(brief_text) -> GateResult; plan_preflight(plan, *, state_dir) -> GateResult; suite_green_zero_reg(report) -> GateResult; posture_locked(*, state_dir) -> GateResult; PROCEDURE_REGISTRY (mode name -> ordered phases, each phase binds a gate name + next-action string); advance(procedure, phase, gate_result) -> Decision (next phase | Blocked(reason, fix_hint) | Complete); ProcedureState(phase: str, last_gate: GateResult | None); load_state(conversation_id, *, state_dir) -> ProcedureState; save_state(conversation_id, state, *, state_dir) -> None.

child_briefs.title: Runtime wiring: per-turn gate execution and the agent-boundary PreToolUse hook
child_briefs.scope: Wire the procedure machine into the live overseer loop, one file per leaf. (1) EDIT overseer/turn_runner.py::run_chat_turn — each turn: load the procedure_state for the conversation, run the CURRENT phase's bound gate via the injected seams (run_seam, git_seam, fs/state_dir), advance the phase with the reducer and persist the new state, and thread the procedure state into render_mode_context so the computed next action and last-gate result surface every turn; preserve all existing per-turn behaviour and tests. (2) NEW overseer/procedure_hook.py — the PreToolUse hook entrypoint on the overseer's claude invocation that DENIES a raw tool call inconsistent with the active phase (the agent-boundary hard-block), e.g. a Write to a brief_hooks_* path while the phase is before BRIEF, or any git commit proxy before the oracle is RED, closing the gap where the jailed agent bypasses the structured action seam with a raw tool; ship the settings fragment wiring the hook onto the overseer's claude invocation. The deterministic hook logic is pure/stdlib-only over the substrate's state and gate names. Extend tests/overseer/test_turn_runner.py and author tests/overseer/test_procedure_hook.py (new) as the per-leaf verification_command targets.
child_briefs.non_goals: Do NOT author or modify the substrate modules or the enforcement edits (can_switch, dispatch_action, render_mode_context) — consume them. No new agent spawns, model/API/network/SSE calls, or un-injected subprocesses; the hook performs deterministic deny decisions only and does not itself execute tests or shell out un-injected. No changes to harness/** or the autowork daemon, and no change to the harness build pipeline. No procedures or registry entries for the out-of-scope modes. The run_chat_turn edit is an EXISTING-symbol additive integration that preserves all current behaviour and tests; the hook is a new single-file whole-file module. Each leaf edits/creates exactly ONE file. This child does not dispatch a build or author the production oracles; the owner gate stays paused.
child_briefs.inputs: From procedure_substrate: PROCEDURE_REGISTRY; advance(procedure, phase, gate_result) -> Decision (next phase | Blocked(reason, fix_hint) | Complete); GateResult(ok: bool, reason: str, fix_hint: str); ProcedureState(phase: str, last_gate: GateResult | None); load_state(conversation_id, *, state_dir) -> ProcedureState; save_state(conversation_id, state, *, state_dir) -> None; the six gate functions oracle_is_red/oracles_committed_at_head/brief_lint/plan_preflight/suite_green_zero_reg/posture_locked invoked via injected seams. From enforcement_integration: the updated render_mode_context(mode, state) that consumes procedure state, and dispatch_action(mode, command, args, *, seams) with its (phase, command) fail-closed check. The ALREADY-BUILT seams: overseer/turn_runner.py::run_chat_turn and the overseer's claude PreToolUse settings surface.
child_briefs.deliverables: Edited overseer/turn_runner.py whose run_chat_turn loads procedure state, runs the current phase's gate through injected seams, advances and persists the phase, and threads the state into render_mode_context each turn. New overseer/procedure_hook.py exposing the PreToolUse hook entrypoint that denies raw tool calls inconsistent with the active phase, plus the settings fragment wiring it onto the overseer's claude invocation. Oracles tests/overseer/test_turn_runner.py (extended) and tests/overseer/test_procedure_hook.py (new), each named as a leaf verification_command python -m pytest tests/overseer/<oracle>.py -q.
child_briefs.interfaces: Consumes PROCEDURE_REGISTRY; advance(procedure, phase, gate_result) -> Decision; GateResult(ok: bool, reason: str, fix_hint: str); ProcedureState(phase: str, last_gate: GateResult | None); load_state(conversation_id, *, state_dir) -> ProcedureState; save_state(conversation_id, state, *, state_dir) -> None; render_mode_context(mode, state). Edits run_chat_turn additively (preserving its signature and behaviour) and produces overseer/procedure_hook.py with a PreToolUse hook entrypoint plus its settings fragment.
